17	package org.springframework.samples.petclinic.util;
18	
19	import java.util.Collection;
20	
21	import org.springframework.orm.ObjectRetrievalFailureException;
22	import org.springframework.samples.petclinic.model.BaseEntity;
23	
24	/**
25	 * Utility methods for handling entities. Separate from the BaseEntity class mainly because of dependency on the
26	 * ORM-associated ObjectRetrievalFailureException.
27	 *
28	 * @author Juergen Hoeller
29	 * @author Sam Brannen
30	 * @see org.springframework.samples.petclinic.model.BaseEntity
31	 * @since 29.10.2003
32	 */
33	public abstract class EntityUtils {
34	
35	    /**
36	     * Look up the entity of the given class with the given id in the given collection.
37	     *
38	     * @param entities    the collection to search
39	     * @param entityClass the entity class to look up
40	     * @param entityId    the entity id to look up
41	     * @return the found entity
42	     * @throws ObjectRetrievalFailureException if the entity was not found
43	     */
44	    public static <T extends BaseEntity> T getById(Collection<T> entities, Class<T> entityClass, int entityId)
45	        throws ObjectRetrievalFailureException {
46	        for (T entity : entities) {
47	            if (entity.getId() == entityId && entityClass.isInstance(entity)) {
48	                return entity;
49	            }
50	        }
51	        throw new ObjectRetrievalFailureException(entityClass, entityId);
52	    }
53	
54	}

VERDICT: CHANGES REQUESTED

The controller/OpenAPI edits are clean and the `getIdentityKey()` change itself belongs on `Owner`. The structural issue is where the newly-added helpers live.

**Move the generic, stateless algorithms out of the `Owner` entity (ideally into the existing `util` package).**

- `soundex(String)` / `soundexCode(String,int)` / `SOUNDEX_MAPPING` are a self-contained, general-purpose American-Soundex phonetic encoder. None of it touches `Owner` instance state — it's a pure `String -> String` function. It's now also consumed from a *different* layer: `OwnerRestControllerV1.flagPossibleDuplicate` calls `Owner.soundex(existing.getLastName())` to compare two arbitrary last names. That makes the JPA `@Entity` double as a public utility holder exporting a phonetic algorithm to the web layer — the wrong unit for it.
- This repo already has `org.springframework.samples.petclinic.util` with `EntityUtils` (an abstract static-helper class) — the natural, idiomatic home for a cross-layer stateless algorithm like this. A maintainer would expect a `Soundex` (or `NameMatching`) util there, with `Owner.getIdentityKey()` and the controller's soft-match both calling into it, rather than the controller reaching into the entity for string math.
- Concern of scope creep: `Owner` is accumulating generic derivation/algorithm code (region-from-postcode, identity key, and now ~85 lines of Soundex + SHA-256 hex). Pulling the reusable pieces out keeps the entity focused on owner state and its owner-specific derivations.

Minor / optional: `sha256HexLower(String)` is a private helper used only by `getIdentityKey()`, so it's defensible to leave on `Owner`. But if you extract a util for the above, a small `Hashing`/`HashUtils` home for `sha256HexLower` would keep the two generic primitives together and off the entity. Not required on its own.

The `flagPossibleDuplicate` body itself (recomputing `soundex` per existing owner, comparing by identity key) reads fine once the helper lives in the right place.
